slides.heading: Clients of Community Health Nurses
slides.subtitle: Who the community health nurse serves — and the concepts of health that guide care.

terms.definition: People who are integrated, interacting and interdependent — the basic unit of service/care.
People sharing common characteristics, developmental stage, or exposure — and thus common health problems.
People sharing common geographic boundaries and/or common values and interests within a specific social system.

slides.heading: Guiding Goals
bullets: Goal of PHC (Primary Health Care): self-reliance in health.
Goal of COPAR: community health development (social transformation).
Health is viewed as a continuum and is the goal of public health / CHN.

terms.definition: Complete physical, mental and social well-being — not merely the absence of disease.
An integrated method of functioning oriented toward maximizing the individual's potential.
Quality of life — social, emotional, mental, spiritual and biological fitness from adaptation to the environment.
Health and illness in relation to the environment.
Soundness and wholeness of human structures and bodily/mental functions.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Four client levels: individual → family → group/population → community.
Family = basic unit of care; individual = entry point.
PHC goal = self-reliance; COPAR goal = social transformation.
Health determinants: genetics, income, education, behavior, health system.
